title: L'Oreal sales rebound as beauty business shifts online in pandemic
主要内容: L'Oreal, the world's largest cosmetics group, reported a rebound in sales during the second half of 2020 as the beauty industry shifted online amid the pandemic. The company's online revenues surged by 62% in 2020, accounting for over a quarter of total sales. This growth was driven by the easing of lockdowns, the reopening of hair salons, and increased consumer demand for skincare and at-home treatments. L'Oreal's sales for the October to December period reached 7.88 billion euros, a 4.8% increase on a like-for-like basis, surpassing market expectations. CEO Jean-Paul Agon noted that the company outperformed the broader beauty market, which saw an 8% decline in 2020. He also expressed confidence in long-term demand for beauty products, comparing the post-pandemic recovery to the 'roaring twenties.' L'Oreal reported a rebound in sales as the beauty business shifted online during the pandemic. The company experienced a 5% drop in net profit for 2020, reaching 3.75 billion euros. L'Oreal also announced a 3.9% increase in its dividend, raising it to 4 euros per share. The company's operating margins remained stable at 18.6%, unchanged from the previous year. This performance highlights the resilience of the beauty sector amid the challenges posed by the pandemic, with a growing emphasis on digital sales channels.
